prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t one clear “best” site that hits all three boxes (beginner plain-English + shows verifiable real numbers + openly publishes losses). Most reputable beginner sites avoid publishing a personal live P&L for legal/ethical reasons. That said, you can get everything you want by using a combination of resources:

Recommendations and why they help
- Coinbase Learn / Binance Academy — plain-English, step‑by‑step explainers for absolute beginners (what crypto is, wallets, keys, simple use cases). Good foundation, but they won’t publish a personal trading P&L.
- Coin Bureau and Crypto Casey (YouTube/website) — long-form plain-English explainers that are well structured and beginner friendly. Again, educational rather than personal performance reporting.
- Dune Analytics — community dashboards built on on‑chain data. Creators publish exact numbers (transactions, positions, protocol flows) and you can verify everything on-chain. Many dashboards show strategy outcomes including losses if the author chooses to include them. This is the closest you’ll find to “real numbers” + transparency.
- Glassnode / Coin Metrics / CryptoQuant — professional on‑chain analytics platforms that publish raw data, charts, and methodology. They don’t run a teaching site in plain English, but they give verifiable numbers (useful once you know the basics).
- Transparent creators who publish wallet addresses (examples: some DeFi tutorial creators like “DeFi Dad”) — these creators perform real transactions with public wallet addresses you can inspect on‑chain. When they publish mistakes or exploits, you can verify the transaction history yourself. (Note: always verify the wallet/address yourself; creator reputations vary.)

What to look for if “publishes losses” is your priority
- Verified wallet addresses or transaction links you can check on an explorer.
- Dashboards or reports that include both winners and losers (look for explicit P&L tables).
- Open methodology and raw data (so you or others can reproduce results).
- Audit or third‑party verification if the site runs paid strategies/products.

If you tell me whether you want to learn trading, long-term investing, or DeFi (smart-contract interactions), I can pick the best single combo of plain-English guides + a few Dune/Glassnode dashboards and specific transparent creators you can follow — and I’ll include direct links and example dashboards that show losses and how they report them.
